issues: No sign of anyone getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and nothing is pasted in. The only test data used is the test fingerprints, through the K_test similarity row, and only to choose the 300 most similar training molecules. Test labels are never read. Fitting a separate model near each test point is allowed.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. K_train[np.ix_(idx, idx)] and K_test[i, idx] index the same training subset, and k = min(300, n) guards against small folds. The fit uses the standardized rank-transformed target, as in the incumbent. Spearman depends only on rank order, so mixing predictions from different local models changes how the method behaves, but the score is still valid.

Recomputed z: (0.4830 - 0.504) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) = -0.021 / 0.0099 = -2.12. This matches the harness value of -2.117. The negative sign means the candidate is worse: its loss of 0.504 is above the incumbent's 0.4830. Rejecting it is correct.
Side note: one SVR fit for each test molecule makes the code more complex and slower, and it does not help. Even if the scores had been equal, the simplicity rule would favour the incumbent.
